14	CASE OD2-HO-CROSS-2 (CROSS, cross-domain): Mould on arrival: rejected mandarin containers at Serra Vale Growers' Cooperative
15	Setting: Serra Vale Growers' Cooperative (fictional) packs mandarins from about 140 member growers in three districts (Lower Serra, Upper Serra, Coastal Flats) and exports them to a single importer, Nordhafen Fresh Imports. This season it used two ocean carriers: Meridane Line (cheaper, transships at Port Calder) and Coastway Shipping (direct sailing). Several changes landed in late July and early August: a new postharvest fungicide supplier (Pellacor), storms over Lower Serra, a new packhouse night-shift supervisor, and a new export documentation suite (Tallis) for Meridane bookings.
16	Presenting request: Five of the nine containers shipped between 1 Aug and 5 Sep were rejected on arrival for mould decay above the contract tolerance. The importer has warned that one more rejection will trigger a review of the season's program. The general manager wants to suspend Lower Serra growers and claim against Meridane. The quality manager wants to go back to the old fungicide. The board asks what caused the rejections and what should be done before the next sailings.
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Nordhafen Fresh Imports, arrival inspection summary (customer-account): Arrival inspection summary from Nordhafen Fresh Imports, sent 2 Oct. Contract tolerance: decay at arrival not above 3% of fruit. K1 (Meridane, sailed 1 Aug) 1.4%, accepted. K2 (Coastway, 4 Aug) 1.1%, accepted. K3 (Meridane, 8 Aug) 11.2%, REJECTED. K4 (Meridane, 15 Aug) 9.4%, REJECTED. K5 (Coastway, 18 Aug) 1.9%, accepted. K6 (Meridane, 22 Aug) 13.8%, REJECTED. K7 (Coastway, 29 Aug) 0.8%, accepted. K8 (Meridane, 29 Aug) 10.6%, REJECTED. K9 (Meridane, 5 Sep) 12.5%, REJECTED. Decay: green and blue mould. Pallet survey, rejected containers only: pallets with Lower Serra grower codes averaged 15.1% decay, other pallets 10.3%. Stowage positions not recorded. A further rejection will trigger a review of the season's program.
19	E2 [stage S1] Packhouse exit QC log, summary prepared by QA clerk (log): Packhouse exit QC log, summary for K1–K9. All nine containers: decay at packing-line exit 0.2–0.5% (spec: not above 1%). Pulp temperature at container loading 3.6–4.3°C for every container, against the cooperative's export carriage specification of 4°C. Postharvest fungicide: Pellacor (new supplier) delivered 2 Aug and in use from that date; the previous supplier's remaining drums were used alongside it until about 12 Aug. Per-container drum records are held in the packing system. Lower Serra deliveries usually arrived after 16:00 and were packed on the night shift throughout August. Night-shift supervisor changed on 3 Aug.
20	E3 [stage S1] Email, D. Achterberg (Quality Manager) to H. Voss (General Manager), 3 Oct (manager-account): 'Helena, the timing is hard to ignore. Procurement moved us to Pellacor to save 18% on fungicide, and the drums arrived on 2 August. K1 and K2 were packed before then and both passed. Since then we have lost five of seven. The Coastway containers that passed are on a direct sailing, so my reading is that the weaker product holds up on a short trip but not on Meridane's transshipment route. Green and blue mould is exactly what a failing fungicide looks like. I recommend we go back to the old supplier immediately, whatever it costs.'
21	E4 [stage S1] Memo, H. Voss (General Manager) to the board, 6 Oct (leadership-account): 'Two issues. First, Nordhafen's own pallet survey shows Lower Serra fruit is the worst in every failed container. Those growers picked straight after the late-July storms against our field officers' advice. I propose suspending Lower Serra deliveries for the rest of the season and withholding their August payments pending review. Second, every rejected container went on Meridane. Their reply that the units ran to our instructed setpoint is what any carrier would say. I have asked our broker to prepare a cargo claim for all five rejected containers on the basis of refrigeration failure.'
22	E5 [stage S1] Interview notes, P. Lemaire (logistics coordinator), 6 Oct (staff-account): Since 4 Aug, Meridane bookings go through the new Tallis export documentation suite, which submits shipping instructions to Meridane's portal electronically. 'It pulls the product details from the master file, so I don't retype anything.' Coastway is not connected yet; their bookings still go by email using the old spreadsheet template, with a move to Tallis planned for November. The implementation contractor, Brindle Systems, set up the master file in the week before go-live. Meridane routes via transshipment at Port Calder, usually 24–27 days; Coastway sails direct, usually 21–25 days. 'Meridane is cheaper, so we put more on them.'
23	E6 [stage S1] Letter, Meridane Line claims desk, 3 Oct (vendor-account): Reply to the cooperative's notice of rejection. 'We have reviewed the voyages for K3, K4, K6, K8 and K9. Our refrigerated units operated to the setpoint stated in your shipping instructions throughout carriage, and no equipment alarms were raised at sea or during transshipment. We do not accept liability for the condition of the cargo on arrival. Controller downloads can be provided on formal request through your broker.'
24	CATALOGUE (full contents)
25	C1 [stage S1] Pellacor certificate of analysis and product data sheet - Pellacor supplier technical department (vendor-account): Certificate of analysis, batch PL-0726, issued 30 Jul: active ingredient content 99.1% of label claim; pH and appearance within specification. Product data sheet: registered for postharvest use on citrus; same active-ingredient class as the cooperative's previous product. 'Supplier trials show efficacy equivalent to leading market products against green and blue mould when applied at label rate.' No independent trial data attached.
26	C2 [stage S1] District rainfall records, 1 Jul–15 Sep - Regional weather service stations (external-data): Daily rainfall totals by station. Lower Serra station: 118 mm over 24–27 Jul, the largest four-day total of the season. Upper Serra station: 46 mm over the same days. Coastal Flats station: 39 mm. All three stations recorded under 5 mm in total between 28 Jul and 15 Sep. Relative humidity at Lower Serra stayed above 85% for four days after the storms, then returned to the seasonal average.
27	C3 [stage S1] Tallis go-live checklist and test sign-off, phase 1 - Cooperative IT project file (document): Go-live checklist, phase 1, signed 3 Aug. Tested and passed: commercial invoice, packing list, certificate-of-origin fields, customs tariff codes, consignee details, document printing. Marked 'out of scope, phase 2': reefer temperature, ventilation and humidity fields. Note: 'Carrier portal validates reefer data on receipt (Brindle advice); scope agreed by steering group 22 Jul.' Open issues at go-live: three, all print layout. Training: four cooperative staff attended on 28 Jul. Coastway integration scheduled for November.
28	C4 [stage S1] Packhouse fungicide tank concentration checks, 2 Aug–5 Sep - Packhouse QA (log): Twice-daily titration checks on the postharvest fungicide tank. 41 checks in the period; 38 within the target band. Three low readings on the 11 Aug night shift (line 2), between 78% and 85% of target, corrected by top-up within an hour. The log does not record which pallets or lots passed through line 2 during the low readings. Checks cover whichever product was in the tank; product identity is not recorded per check.
29	C5 [stage S1] Port Calder terminal reefer plug-in records for Meridane transshipments - Port Calder terminal operator (system-record): Terminal reefer monitoring extract, Meridane transshipments 10 Aug–22 Sep, covering K1, K3, K4, K6, K8 and K9. Dwell at Port Calder: 2–4 days per container. Each unit was plugged in within 35 minutes of discharge and stayed connected until loading onto the onward vessel. The terminal system records plug status and alarm flags only, not temperatures; no alarm flags were raised for any of the six units.
30	C6 [stage S1] Container controller temperature downloads and packing records, K1–K9 - Carrier controller downloads compiled by cooperative QA (telemetry): Controller downloads from both carriers on formal request; co-op QA added each container's packing record and cross-checked its own pallet loggers in K4, K5 and K6 (agreement within 0.3°C). Columns: controller setpoint; mean return-air °C; transit days; fungicide stock; arrival decay.

32	K2: 4.0; 4.2; 22; old; 1.1%
33	K3: 7.0; 7.1; 25; old; 11.2%
34	K4: 7.0; 7.0; 23; Pellacor; 9.4%

38	K8: 7.0; 6.9; 24; Pellacor; 10.6%
39	K9: 7.0; 7.1; 25; Pellacor; 12.5%
40	No unit logged a power-off longer than 40 minutes or a deviation from setpoint above 0.4°C. Lower Serra fruit made up 28–40% of each container. Pallet-level decay was not surveyed in accepted containers.
41	C7 [stage S1] Importer's laboratory report on decayed fruit samples - Nordhafen contract laboratory (expert-account): Samples from K3, K6 and K9, 40 decayed fruit each. Organisms isolated: Penicillium digitatum (green mould) in 71% of fruit, P. italicum (blue mould) in 24%, mixed in 5%. Both are common postharvest wound pathogens of citrus. Lesions were at mixed stages of development, consistent with infections that progressed during carriage rather than at a single point. Fungicide residue testing was not requested and was not performed.
42	C8 [stage S1] Receival intake grading by grower district, 29 Jul–5 Sep - Cooperative receival station (system-record): Intake grading of grower bins by district. Rain blemish and split rate in sampled fruit: Lower Serra 6.8%; Upper Serra 2.1%; Coastal Flats 1.7%. Bins exceeding the receival limit for splits are diverted to juice before packing; 9% of Lower Serra bins were diverted, against 2% from the other districts. Lower Serra share of packed export volume over the period: 31%.
43	C9 [stage S1] Board minutes approving the fungicide supplier change, 18 Jun - Cooperative board secretary (document): Item 6: Procurement proposed moving postharvest fungicide supply to Pellacor from the August deliveries, citing an 18% saving and same active-ingredient class. Quality Manager noted that no in-house trial had been run and asked for one; procurement replied that supplier efficacy data would be provided and that registration covers citrus. Motion carried, one abstention. Action: procurement to place the first order for delivery in early August.
44	C10 [stage S1] Interview with the packhouse night-shift supervisor - Interview notes, T. Nakamura, night-shift supervisor since 3 Aug (staff-account): 'Lower Serra bins come in late, so we run most of them at night. Some bins had more splits after the storms, and we sort those to juice. The crew was new to me but line speeds are the same as on days, and the fungicide tank is on the same schedule.' She said nobody told the night shift about any rejections until 2 Oct, and she had not seen arrival reports. She asked for more sorters on Lower Serra runs in mid-August; request still pending.
45	C11 [stage S1] Transmitted shipping instructions K1–K9 and Tallis product-master change history - Extract by cooperative IT, 9 Oct (change-record): K1 (Meridane): booked 28 Jul by email on the spreadsheet template, carriage temperature 4.0°C. K2, K5, K7 (Coastway): email template, 4.0°C. K3, K4, K6, K8, K9 (Meridane): submitted by Tallis to Meridane's portal, carriage temperature 7.0°C, populated automatically from product record PRD-MAND-01. Change history: PRD-MAND-01 created 1 Aug by user brindle.impl as a copy of PRD-AVO-01 (avocado, 7.0°C); description and tariff code edited, temperature field unchanged; no later edits. Cooperative product specification, mandarins: carriage 4.0°C. Go-live sign-off 3 Aug, 'product master reviewed': R. Okafor, cooperative logistics lead. Pending on PRD-MAND-01: one Meridane container sailed 3 Oct (at sea), one queued for 10 Oct.
46	C12 [stage S1] Export rejection history, previous two seasons - Cooperative export office (prior-report): Season before last: 24 containers to Nordhafen, no rejections. Last season: 27 containers, one rejection (decay 4.1%), recorded at the time as linked to a nine-day vessel delay. Carriers used in both seasons: Coastway and a third carrier no longer serving the route. Meridane was first used this season after a tender won on price. Average arrival decay in accepted containers over both seasons: 1.2%.
47	C13 [stage S1] Forced-air pre-cooling room logs for K1–K9 lots - Packhouse cold store (log): Pre-cooling logs for all pallets loaded into K1–K9. Every pallet reached the 4°C target pulp temperature within 7–10 hours of entering the forced-air room. Cold-store holding before loading was 0–2 days at 3–5°C. Two short door-open alarms (under 15 minutes) on 14 Aug and 27 Aug, both cleared without temperature excursion beyond 5°C. No differences in cooling time by grower district were recorded.
48	C14 [stage S1] Lower Serra growers' spray and harvest diaries, July–August - Grower diaries collected by field officers (document): Diaries from 14 Lower Serra growers. Harvest paused during the storms of 24–27 Jul and resumed between 29 and 31 Jul. Nine of the 14 recorded a preharvest fungicide spray within the label interval before the storms; five recorded none. Field officers' advice to wait three dry days before picking was followed by six growers. Bins picked on the first day after the storms were flagged on delivery dockets by four growers.
49	C15 [stage S1] Freight rate comparison, Meridane and Coastway, current season - Cooperative finance office (financial-record): Contracted ocean freight per 40-foot reefer container to Nordhafen: Meridane 14% below Coastway including the transshipment surcharge. Volume this season to date: Meridane 6 containers, Coastway 3. Projected annual saving from the Meridane allocation: about 9% of the freight budget. Payment terms: Meridane 45 days, Coastway 30 days. No disputed invoices with either carrier this season.
50	CANDIDATES
51	H1: The rejections arose because the postharvest fungicide from the new supplier protects the fruit less well than the previous product.
52	H2: The rejections arose because rain-affected fruit from Lower Serra growers carried infection into the export containers.
53	H3: The rejections arose because Meridane's refrigerated units or handling failed to keep the containers at the temperature the cooperative instructed.
54	H4: The rejections arose because the cooperative's own shipping instructions, after the move to the new documentation suite, specified a carriage temperature unsuitable for mandarins.
55	H5: The rejections arose because Meridane's transshipment routing kept the fruit in transit longer than it can tolerate.
56	R1: Meridane bookings moved to the Tallis documentation suite -> Temperature setpoint on Meridane mandarin containers (determined)
57	R2: Container temperature during the voyage -> Mould decay above the 3% tolerance on arrival (drives)
58	R3: Switch to the new supplier's fungicide -> Mould decay above the 3% tolerance on arrival (causes)
59	R4: Lower Serra grower lots -> Higher pallet-level decay within rejected containers (causes)
60	A1: Lodge a cargo claim against Meridane for the five rejected containers on the basis of refrigeration failure.
61	A2: Suspend Lower Serra deliveries for the rest of the season and withhold their August payments.
62	A3: Correct the carriage temperature held in the Tallis mandarin product record to the cooperative's specification, have Meridane reset any queued or at-sea mandarin container to that temperature, and add a pre-submission check comparing reefer settings with the product specification.
63	A4: Deduct the value of the five rejected containers from Brindle Systems' final implementation invoice on the grounds that its staff created the faulty product data.
64	A5: Place independent temperature loggers in every export container for the rest of the season.
65	SCORED ITEMS

Fungicide residue testing was not requested and was not performed.

Bins exceeding the receival limit for splits are diverted to juice before packing; 9% of Lower Serra bins were diverted, against 2% from the other districts. Lower Serra share of packed export volume over the period: 31%.

H1: The rejections arose because the postharvest fungicide from the new supplier protects the fruit less well than the previous product.
H2: The rejections arose because rain-affected fruit from Lower Serra growers carried infection into the export containers.
H3: The rejections arose because Meridane's refrigerated units or handling failed to keep the containers at the temperature the cooperative instructed.
H4: The rejections arose because the cooperative's own shipping instructions, after the move to the new documentation suite, specified a carriage temperature unsuitable for mandarins.
H5: The rejections arose because Meridane's transshipment routing kept the fruit in transit longer than it can tolerate.
R1: Meridane bookings moved to the Tallis documentation suite -> Temperature setpoint on Meridane mandarin containers (determined)
R2: Container temperature during the voyage -> Mould decay above the 3% tolerance on arrival (drives)

R4: Lower Serra grower lots -> Higher pallet-level decay within rejected containers (causes)

A2: Suspend Lower Serra deliveries for the rest of the season and withhold their August payments.
A3: Correct the carriage temperature held in the Tallis mandarin product record to the cooperative's specification, have Meridane reset any queued or at-sea mandarin container to that temperature, and add a pre-submission check comparing reefer settings with the product specification.
A4: Deduct the value of the five rejected containers from Brindle Systems' final implementation invoice on the grounds that its staff created the faulty product data.
A5: Place independent temperature loggers in every export container for the rest of the season.

answers.justification: In C6, K3 was treated with the old fungicide and was still rejected at a 7.0°C setpoint, while K5 and K7 were treated with Pellacor and passed at 4.0°C; C1 and C4 show no product or tank failure that lines up with the rejections.

Lower Serra fruit made up 28–40% of every container, including the accepted ones (C6, C8). Non-Lower Serra pallets in the rejected containers were still at 10.3% (E1), so rain-affected fruit cannot explain the split between rejected and accepted containers, even if it adds to decay.

C6 shows return air within 0.4°C of setpoint and no long power-offs, the co-op's own loggers agreed within 0.3°C, and C5 shows prompt plug-in and no alarms at Port Calder; the units held the temperature they were instructed to hold (E6).

C11 shows that every Tallis-submitted Meridane booking carried 7.0°C, copied from the avocado record PRD-AVO-01, against the 4.0°C mandarin specification. In C6, all five 7.0°C containers were rejected and all four 4.0°C containers passed, whatever the fungicide or carrier.
K1 went on Meridane, took 26 days and passed at 4.0°C; K5 took 26 days on Coastway and passed; K4 took only 23 days and was rejected at 7.0°C (C6). Transit time does not separate the outcomes.

C11 shows the mechanism: Tallis filled the temperature automatically from PRD-MAND-01, which was copied from the avocado record at 7.0°C and never edited. It also gives a contrast: K1 went to Meridane by email before the switch and was set at 4.0°C, while Tallis-booked Meridane containers were all set at 7.0°C. C3 shows reefer fields were left out of testing.

In C6, setpoint separates the outcomes perfectly, with fungicide, carrier and transit time all varying across both groups. C7 shows lesions progressed during carriage, and warmer temperatures plausibly speed up Penicillium growth, which supports a natural-experiment reading.
K3 used the old fungicide and failed, while K5 and K7 used Pellacor and passed (C6); tank concentrations were mostly in band and the brief low readings were corrected (C4).

E1 shows higher decay on Lower Serra pallets, and C8 and C14 give a plausible wound-and-rain mechanism. But stowage positions were not recorded, accepted containers were not surveyed (E1, C6), and night-shift packing is a confounder, so causation is not established.

The carrier ran the units to the setpoint the cooperative itself instructed (C6, C11, E6), so a refrigeration-failure claim is baseless, would cost money and would damage the carrier relationship by blaming the wrong party.

Suspending Lower Serra growers and withholding their payments punishes them for a failure driven by the 7.0°C setpoint (C6, C11). Lower Serra fruit also went into the accepted containers, and the diversion of split fruit to juice is already working (C8).

C11 shows one container at sea and one queued for 10 Oct on the faulty 7.0°C record, and one more rejection triggers a program review (E1). Correcting the record, resetting those containers and adding a check fixes the established cause directly.

Brindle created the faulty record (C11), but the cooperative signed off 'product master reviewed' and its steering group agreed to leave reefer fields out of testing (C3, C11). Contractual liability is unclear, so a unilateral deduction is not yet justified.

Independent loggers are a reasonable check for the rest of the season, but the cause is already identified, and the controller data already matched the co-op's own loggers (C6), so this is not among the best actions.
C6, C11 and C3 together establish the 7.0°C setpoint error, its source and its link to the rejections, which is enough to commit to A3 now.

ambiguousItems: I-A4: premature vs harmful. The cooperative shares fault through Okafor's sign-off and the scope decision (C3, C11), so a deduction could be read as punishing the wrong party.
I-R4: association-only vs causal. C8 and C14 give a plausible mechanism, but stowage and night-shift confounders are not ruled out.
I-H2: contradicted vs unknown. Lower Serra fruit may have added to decay within containers, but it does not explain which containers were rejected.
caseProblems: C6 puts the setpoint column next to fungicide stock and arrival decay in a single table, which comes close to handing over the answer; C11 then spells out the avocado-copy mechanism explicitly.
K5 (Coastway) shows a 26-day transit, above Coastway's stated usual range of 21–25 days (E5). This looks engineered to break the transit-time confound.

E1 reports all five rejections only on 2 Oct, although the containers arrived in late August and September. In reality an importer would normally report each rejection on arrival. C10 says the night shift heard nothing until 2 Oct, which is consistent with E1 but implausible.
C15 says Meridane has carried 6 containers 'to date', which leaves out the container that sailed 3 Oct and is at sea (C11). This is minor.
